blocks.text: MS is an immune-mediated disease in which the protective myelin around nerve fibres in the brain and spinal cord is damaged, slowing or blocking nerve signals. It is most often diagnosed in young adults, more often in women. Types: **relapsing-remitting** (attacks followed by recovery), **secondary progressive** (gradual worsening after a relapsing phase) and **primary progressive** (gradual worsening from onset).

Symptoms depend on lesion location: fatigue (very common), weakness, spasticity, sensory change, balance and coordination problems, visual problems (optic neuritis), bladder and bowel urgency, pain, cognitive and mood changes. **Heat sensitivity (Uhthoff phenomenon)**: symptoms temporarily worsen with raised body temperature, then recover on cooling.

Type of MS and disease duration; recent relapses; fatigue pattern (worst time of day); heat sensitivity; falls; bladder urgency (affects exercise planning); walking distance; work and family roles; goals.

sections.title: D to E. Examination and measures

blocks.text: Also assess tone, strength, coordination (finger-nose, heel-shin), sensation, and vision.

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: New or worsening symptoms lasting more than 24 hours without fever
Worsening with fever or urinary symptoms
Sudden vision loss with eye pain

steps: **Relapse?** Reduce intensity, maintain function, wait for recovery, then re-assess.
**Stable:** exercise program (aerobic, resistance, balance), fatigue management.
**Progressive with high disability:** maintain mobility, transfers, prevent contracture, equipment, carer training.

items: **Aerobic exercise**: moderate intensity, for example 10 to 30 minutes, 2 to 3 times a week, progressing [Ref – to verify].
**Resistance training**: major muscle groups, 2 times a week, 1 to 3 sets of 8 to 15 repetitions.
**Balance training**: progressive, task-specific, including dual tasks.

**Heat management**: cool environment, fans, cooling vests, cold drinks, exercise early in the day. **Fatigue management**: energy conservation (plan, prioritise, pace), rest breaks, sleep hygiene. Exercise reduces fatigue in many people [Ref – to verify].
**Spasticity**: daily stretching, positioning, standing; medical treatment if severe.
**Ataxia**: core stability, coordination exercises, weighted aids in some cases.

items: **What is Uhthoff phenomenon?** Temporary worsening of symptoms with increased body temperature.
**How can you help a heat-sensitive patient exercise?** Cool environment, cooling vests, cold drinks, shorter intervals.
**What distinguishes relapse from pseudo-relapse?** Pseudo-relapse is triggered by infection or heat and resolves when the trigger resolves.
**Does exercise worsen MS?** No. Appropriate exercise improves fitness, strength, mobility and often fatigue.
**What strategy reduces fatigue in daily life?** Energy conservation: plan, prioritise and pace.
